finding: No existing guarded lane A route admits a native guest SEO run against the exact development artifact.

evidence.fact: planHostedGuestSeo requires lane B, case guest-seo, exact scope notice-stacked, fixture none, resource diagnostic false, interruption none, and runner macos-15-intel. It plans workflow_dispatch with those values and development artifact IDs.
planHostedScrape requires lane B, case guest-scrape-development, scope seo-schema-empty, guest auth and macos-15-intel. It plans the development artifact route.

The workflow exposes additional SEO scopes (full, controlled, notice, readability, metadata and narrow), but its lane predicates and fixture/diagnostic conditions do not establish a lane A admission. The normal local SEO helper rejects these wider scopes.

guest_seo_normal_admission.meaning: Two owned refusal notices, Re-audit hit testing and dismissal/cleanup; this is fixture behavior and supplies no broad SEO audit or SEO control coverage.

guest_scrape_development_normal_admissio.meaning: Owned localhost T08 no-signal SEO and empty Schema panes only.

unresolved_source_level_question: The source enforces lane B for these guest routes, while the plan says lane A owns shared authenticated fixtures. Available code does not establish whether the guest-only B restriction exists for host/resource isolation, fixture or credential ownership, or exact-case policy. A future route change should first establish this rationale; do not infer that guest SEO work is safe on lane A from the current predicates alone.
decision: Do not redispatch this lane A task through an alternate command or workflow path. Any meaningful exact-artifact guest SEO route requires a separately reviewed admission change and lane/resource coordination.
